title: Prove and bind the stronger ordinary rate at c=1/577
body:
The completed ordinary backend's proof fixes `c=17/10000`, giving saving `.00169711`, below PR2979's stated complex endpoint. I prove and bind the stronger coupling **`c=1/577`**, giving ordinary saving **`a=576/332929 ≈ .0017300986096`** under the retained source/refinement and physical-cost premises. This exceeds that complex endpoint by about `1.0646e-6`; I do not claim a new multiplication exponent.

The compiled Profile API already supports this parameter. The missing step was a uniform theorem for its actual producer: the old moment bound below `.9999` fails at the new point. I retain the complete BIT fallback surcharge and certify the new moment below `.999999` with two exact engines. I derive the C0 bound `200 C n + 1000000 C n^(576/577) w`, preserve the history and physical reserve estimates, and prove eventual fit of the actual original-width stock selector for `e>=2^20`. I charge both padded returns and the complete added wrapper bill, obtaining coefficient `4283584 C` in the ordinary time bound.

I add an opt-in ordinary/binary factory backed by an authenticated, unchanged export of PR2899. I retain the original compatible stock, covering rule and shared defaults. I do not combine the newer strict-padding or smaller-stock adapters.

I verified head `abb93be8b9ceca07a2b17f3a97db7bb6b074271d` with CPython 3.12.13 and the standard library:

- Four registered optimized checks passed: exact moment/constant certificates, literal Count setup, actual physical returns and actual CLI source controls.
- The physical fixtures cover 192 ordinary-fallback columns, 16 binary columns and a declared reduced 256-column ordinary exchange with two 384-column padded C0 returns. I check each return before cancellation, borrowed inputs, cleanup and reuse. The declared plan is not a selected-profile fit or GL64 execution.
- Committed-byte/source-history checks passed for 17 package/input files. All four commands passed from a Git-free export, and I compared all 18 exported regular files byte-for-byte afterward.
- I confirmed successful planning and package replay for this head in [GitHub CI run39102265160](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39102265160).

I start from canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. I state the quantified contract in [PROOF.md](https://github.com/jmbarrancoml/integer-mult-bounds/blob/abb93be8b9ceca07a2b17f3a97db7bb6b074271d/research/retuned-ordinary-coupling/PROOF.md) and record finite coverage and corrected development diagnostics in [EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/jmbarrancoml/integer-mult-bounds/blob/abb93be8b9ceca07a2b17f3a97db7bb6b074271d/research/retuned-ordinary-coupling/EVIDENCE.md). Reviewers still need to check the inherited all-size source-to-physical and cost premises. The T74 stopping/root parameters, production consumer binding and modern outer integration remain separate. I leave the selected frontier unchanged.

I retain David Arias/PR2753, Nick Petalas/PR2808 and the stock/selector lineage, Adam Gall/PR2087, Gareth Davidson/PR2289, PR2399, my PR2809/2899/2915 physical backend, PR3342's interval engine, and the selected geometry/compiler notices. The bootstrap formula and ordinary identity are predecessor results. Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, code, checks and prose. [Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-19012323).

I refreshed overlap through 2026-10-18 05:55:39 UTC, with complete coverage of 278 open PRs and 2,397 Discussion records plus current local notes and subsequent PR metadata. I found no matching claim beyond this investigation. I did not inspect arbitrary diffs or unpublished work.
